title: 第264章 审判之焰第三姓名第263章 审判之焰补名
slug: 黯潮纪元异世界的崛起
lines: 空剑冷得粘住了掌心。
陈默低头看着自己的右手——手指和剑柄之间结了一层霜，霜把皮肤和金属冻在一起。他试了三次才把手指掰开，掌心撕掉一小块皮，血渗出来，滴在霜上。霜没化。血珠直接从霜面滚落，沿着剑脊划出一道暗红的线，线没散开，而是渗进霜痕里。
不是普通的冰。
盔甲第四次开口。护喉里吐出的声音比刚才更沉，像声带被火焰烧薄了，只剩一层铁皮在振：“契约编号——瑟兰迪尔·第三纪元·第十三序列·第七星阶——”
又断了。
缺口。胸甲上那个缺口，边缘往外翻的火焰纹路，像一枚被撬走的印章留下的母模。陈默盯着它，膝盖骨压在地砖裂缝上，脊椎里窜过一阵冷——不是恐惧，是考古学家的眼睛在看。
三星堆。青铜神树底座。那根被打断的树枝。
他见过同样的东西：青铜器上被故意磨掉的铭文，磨掉之后留下的凹槽比周围低半毫米，凹槽底部的金属纹理和周围不一样——不是凿掉的，是铸的时候就空出来的。
胸甲上的缺口也是。不是被烧毁的。是铸甲时就预留的空白。
陈默把空剑横过来，剑脊朝上。霜痕在剑脊上排列成行——不是冰，是凹痕。凹痕的走向和盔甲胸甲缺口边缘的压痕一模一样，像一枚印章的正反面。
“补名槽。”陈默说出口，声音干得像砂纸擦过喉咙。
盔甲没回答。护喉里火焰烧了一下，像在等他继续。
地砖上的审判纹路开始动了。纹路从盔甲脚下爬出来，沿着地砖的裂缝往前延伸，像树根在泥土里找水。三条纹路同时向陈默的膝盖爬过来，每爬一寸，地砖就往下沉一截，像整座大厅在陷落。
陈默盯着那三条纹路——它们不是随机延伸。每条纹路都在绕开他膝盖下方的裂缝，绕开之后又汇合，汇合点正对着他的胸口。
锁定。
不是审判。是定位。审判纹路在确定他的坐标。
陈默把空剑插进地砖裂缝。
不是战斗。是测量。剑尖抵住裂缝的底部，剑身斜着立起来，剑脊上的霜痕对准盔甲胸甲的缺口。他在考古现场处理过残碑——残缺的铭文不能用补的，要用拓印，把完整的部分压出来，缺的部分自然就显形了。
空剑是拓片。
霜痕是墨。
盔甲胸甲的缺口是母模。
陈默用左手握住剑刃，用力一拉。掌心被割开，血涌出来，顺着剑脊往下淌。血碰到霜痕时没流走，被凹痕吸进去，像水渗进干裂的河床。霜痕被血染成暗红色，在剑脊上凸起来——不是凹痕了，是凸痕。
凸痕的形状和盔甲胸甲缺口边缘的压痕一模一样。
陈默站起来。膝盖骨咔地响了一声，他差点跪回去——右腿已经完全麻木了，小腿像灌了铅。他咬着牙把重心移到左腿，用剑尖撑住地面，一步，两步，往盔甲走过去。
盔甲没动。护喉里火焰烧着，那层铁皮般的声音压低了五度：“契约编号——”
又断了。但这次断的位置变了——缺口缩小了一毫米。
陈默走到盔甲面前，近到能看清火焰在甲片缝隙里烧出的纹理。他把空剑举起来，剑脊平放，对准胸甲的缺口，慢慢压下去。
剑脊贴上缺口边缘的一刻，火焰像蜡一样凹陷下去。
不是烧。是融化。盔甲胸甲上那层火焰往两侧退开，露出缺口内侧的金属——不是铁，不是钢，是暗灰色的材质，表面布满细密的纹路，像古书的页码。陈默把剑脊完全压进缺口，霜痕和缺口边缘的压痕咬合在一起，严丝合缝。
盔甲不动了。
火焰停了。

The empty sword was so cold that it stuck to the palm of his hand.
Chen Mo looked down at his right hand - there was a layer of frost between the fingers and the sword hilt, and the frost froze the skin and the metal together. It took him three attempts to open his fingers, and a small piece of skin was torn off in his palm. Blood seeped out and dripped on the frost. The frost has not melted. The blood beads rolled down directly from the frost surface, drawing a dark red line along the spine of the sword. The line did not spread out, but seeped into the frost marks.
Not ordinary ice.
Armor spoke for the fourth time. The voice spit out from the gorget was deeper than before, as if the vocal cords had been burned thin by flames, leaving only a layer of iron vibrating: "Contract number - Thranduil, Third Era, Thirteenth Sequence, Seventh Star Level -"
It broke again.
gap. The notch on the breastplate and the flame pattern on the edge are like the mother mold left by a seal that has been pried away. Chen Mo stared at it, his kneecaps pressed against the cracks in the floor tiles, and a chill ran through his spine - it wasn't fear, it was the eyes of an archaeologist watching.
Sanxingdui. Bronze sacred tree base. The broken branch.
He had seen the same thing: an inscription on a bronze vessel that had been deliberately worn away. The groove left after grinding was half a millimeter lower than the surrounding area. The metal texture at the bottom of the groove was different from the surroundings - it was not chiseled off, but vacated during casting.
So are the notches in the breastplate. Not burned. It is the blank space reserved when the armor is cast.
Chen Mo turned his empty sword sideways, with the sword's spine facing upwards. Frost marks lined the sword's spine—not ice, but dents. The direction of the indentation is exactly the same as the indentation on the edge of the notch on the armor's breastplate, like the front and back of a seal.
"Fix the name slot." Chen Mo said, his voice as dry as sandpaper scraping his throat.
Armor didn't answer. The flames burned in the gorget, as if waiting for him to continue.
The judgment patterns on the floor tiles began to move. The lines crawled out from under the armor's feet and extended forward along the cracks in the floor tiles, like tree roots searching for water in the soil. Three stripes of road crawled toward Chen Mo's knees at the same time. With every inch they climbed, the floor tiles sank a little, as if the entire hall was sinking.
Chen Mo stared at the three lines - they were not randomly extended. Each path skirted the crack below his knees, then merged again, right at his chest.
locking.
Not a trial. It's positioning. The judgment pattern is determining his coordinates.
***
Chen Mo inserted the empty sword into the cracks in the floor tiles.
Not a fight. It's measurement. The tip of the sword touched the bottom of the crack, the sword stood up diagonally, and the frost marks on the sword's spine aligned with the gap in the armor's breastplate. He has dealt with broken stele at archaeological sites - incomplete inscriptions cannot be repaired, but rubbings must be used to press out the complete parts, and the missing parts will naturally appear.
The empty sword is a rubbing.
Frost marks are ink.
The notch in the armor's breastplate is the female mold.
Chen Mo held the sword blade with his left hand and pulled hard. The palm of the hand was cut open, blood gushed out and flowed down the spine of the sword. The blood did not flow away when it touched the frost marks, but was sucked into the dents, like water seeping into a cracked river bed. The frost marks were stained dark red by blood, and were raised on the spine of the sword - they were not dents, but convex marks.
The shape of the ridge is exactly the same as the indentation on the edge of the notch on the armor's breastplate.
Chen Mo stood up. His kneecaps clicked, and he almost knelt down - his right leg was completely numb, and his calf felt like lead. He gritted his teeth and shifted his weight to his left leg, supported the ground with the tip of his sword, and walked towards the armor in one step, then two steps.
The armor didn't move. The flames burned in the gorget, and the iron-like voice lowered five degrees: "Contract number——"
It broke again. But this time the location of the break has changed - the gap has shrunk by a millimeter.
Chen Mo walked up to the armor, close enough to see the texture of the flames burning in the gaps between the armor plates. He raised the empty sword, laid the sword spine flat, pointed it at the gap in the breastplate, and slowly pressed it down.
The moment the sword spine touched the edge of the gap, the flame sunk down like wax.
Not burning. It's melting. The layer of flames on the armor's breastplate retreated to both sides, revealing the metal inside the gap - not iron, not steel, but a dark gray material, with fine lines on the surface, like the pages of an ancient book. Chen Mo pressed the sword spine completely into the gap. The frost marks and the indentations on the edge of the gap fit together tightly.
The armor stopped moving.
The flames stopped.
